_comment: bim.export.ar rules (Q6207): what an AR export of the built model keeps, how it colours it and how big it may get. A job overrides any key in its building spec under `ar_export` (same shape); every list and number here is data, not code.

caps.source: AR Quick Look guidance for a phone: a few hundred thousand triangles and tens of MB keep it smooth (owner 11-05 target: 300k triangles, 50 MB)

context.source: the building's shell and structure: shown for orientation, see-through so the trades read through it

skip_parts.source: a room element is a space (its floor outline), not something built

small_parts.source: the trades' loose pieces (studs, sheets, straps, staples, connectors, wire) and anything under 30 mm across: too small to see on a phone, and thousands of them

colors._comment: RGB 0-255 by the element's system (the BIM view's trade keys), then by trade group; `default` for anything else. Context parts use their own colour with the context opacity.
colors.source: the BIM view's trade colour table (bimlook TRADES), so the phone matches the desktop's 3D view

kind_trades.source: a plumbing fixture is plumbing whatever layer its symbol sits on
fire alarm devices are their own trade and system (NFPA 72), shown apart from power

scope.source: an element belongs to a room when its plan box comes within the margin of the room's outline (devices sit on the wall face, the wall straddles it); a door is a room's entry when a probe this far past its far face lands in another room or outside
